name: dashboard_describe
description: Return a compact outline of the current dashboard: sections and widgets with their ids, types, spans and bindings. Call this first whenever you edit an existing dashboard.

name: dashboard_apply
description: Apply a list of edit ops to the dashboard, in order and atomically. If any op fails, or the edit introduces new validation errors, nothing changes and an error with a code and path is returned; validation errors that already existed do not block the edit. Available ops: addSection, removeSection, moveSection, updateSection, addWidget, removeWidget, moveWidget, resizeWidget, updateWidget, updateWidgetData, setWidgetValue, setBinding, clearBinding, setTitle. Use ids from dashboard_describe.

name: dashboard_propose_widget
description: Add one new widget bound to catalog metrics; the widget id is generated for you. Slots per type: kpi: value (value, required); kpi-strip: a (value, required), b (value, required), c (value, optional), d (value, optional); text: none; briefing: none; trend: series (series, required); bar: series (series, required); donut: series (series, required); comparison: a (series, required), b (series, required); funnel: series (series, required); leaderboard: rows (table, required); table: rows (table, required).

sectionId.description: Target section id; defaults to the first section.

span.description: Grid size; omit to use the type default.

bindings.description: Slot name → binding. Bind every required slot of the chosen type.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: KPI
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use for one headline number the reader should see first, such as revenue, signups or error rate. Bind the single `value` slot to one metric; set compare to "previous" on the binding so a change versus the previous period appears, and leave showDelta on. Use emphasis "large" for the single most important number on the dashboard. For two to four related numbers side by side prefer kpi-strip.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: KPI strip
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use for a compact row of two to four related headline numbers, usually at the top of a section. Bind slots a and b (required) and optionally c and d, each to one metric; each tile is labelled with its metric name. Set compare to "previous" on the bindings to show changes. Use kpi instead when a single number deserves emphasis.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Text
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use for static written context: a short explanation of a section, a caveat about the data, or a note for readers. Write the content in `markdown`; it has no data slots, so do not bind anything. For findings generated from the data use briefing instead.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Briefing
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use at the top of a dashboard or section to say in plain language what the data shows. Write `parts` as the lead sentence (mark key figures with strong) and `findings` as two to five short bullets, each with a tone: positive for good news, negative for problems, warning for things to watch, neutral otherwise. Base every number on the bound data of the other widgets. Optionally set `prompt` to a follow-up question; when the host handles asks it becomes an "Ask about this" button. It has no data slots.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Trend
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use to show how one metric moves over time, such as daily revenue or weekly signups. Bind the `series` slot to a metric grouped by a time dimension (day, week or month) so labels are dates; ISO dates are shown as "Oct 5" on the axis. Set compare to "previous" on the binding and turn showPrevious on to draw the previous period as a dashed line for context. Turn area on for volume-like metrics where the filled shape helps; leave it off when comparing against the previous line. For category breakdowns use bar or donut instead.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Bar chart
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use to compare one metric across categories, such as revenue by plan, orders by country or tickets by priority. Bind the `series` slot to a metric grouped by a categorical dimension. Set sort to "desc" for rankings so the biggest category comes first, or keep "none" when the categories have a natural order (sizes, stages, weekdays). Use orientation "horizontal" when category names are long or there are more than about eight of them. For a share of a whole with few categories prefer donut; for change over time prefer trend.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Donut
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use to show how a total splits into parts, such as traffic by source or revenue by plan, when there are about two to six categories. Bind the `series` slot to an additive metric (counts, sums, revenue; never averages or rates) grouped by a categorical dimension; the centre shows the formatted total. Keep showLegend on unless the widget is very small. With more than six categories, or when exact comparison matters more than share, use bar instead.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Comparison
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use to compare two series over the same categories, such as this quarter versus last quarter by region, or two segments by plan. Bind slots `a` and `b` to series with the same format grouped by the same dimension; categories are matched by label and a category missing from one side counts as 0. Set labelA and labelB to short names the reader recognises (for example "This month" and "Last month"); they appear in the legend and tooltip. For a single metric against its own previous period over time prefer trend with showPrevious.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Funnel
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use for a sequence of steps where each one is a subset of the one before, such as visited, signed up, activated, paid. Bind the `series` slot to points in step order, first step first; each bar is drawn relative to the first step. Keep showConversion on so the percentage that made it from each step to the next appears between steps, which is usually the number the reader cares about. Do not use for categories without an order; use bar instead.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Leaderboard
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use for a ranked list of one metric by a dimension, such as top customers by revenue, busiest endpoints or most active users. Bind the `rows` slot to a metric with `by` set to the dimension and `sort: "desc"` so the biggest item comes first (rows render in the order the data source returns them), and set `limit` on both the binding and the widget to the number of rows wanted. Each row shows the label, the formatted value and a bar scaled to the largest value. For a full multi-column listing prefer table; for a visual comparison of many categories prefer bar.

x-dashkit-widgets.label: Table
x-dashkit-widgets.aiHint: Use when the reader needs exact values for many rows, such as a per-customer breakdown or a list of recent records. Bind the `rows` slot to a metric with `by` set to the dimension; the data source decides which columns exist. Leave `columns` empty to show every column, or list column keys in the order they should appear. Turn on dense for long lists. For a ranking of one metric prefer leaderboard; for a visual comparison prefer bar.

name: catalog_search
description: Search catalog metrics and dimensions by key, label or description (case-insensitive substring). Returns up to 20 metrics with their format and allowed dimensions, matching dimensions, and all window presets.

query.description: Text to look for, e.g. "spend" or "per lead".
